title_prefix: An inferred pk_h node carries no key, so
mechanism: ms-from-script emits (make-ms-node :pk-h :data keyhash) with an EMPTY keys list (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1810-1817) because it has no context object to resolve the 20-byte hash back to a key. ms-produce-input's :pk-h arm (:1505-1509) then evaluates (first (ms-node-keys node)) = NIL, calls the satisfier's sign-fn with NIL, and builds the revealed-key element as (ms-stack-of (funcall key-fn NIL)), a stack element whose value is the Lisp NIL. The docstring at :1811-1816 says 'a satisfier looks the key up by it'; no satisfier does -- there is no hash-to-key lookup anywhere in the satisfier or in either of its two callers. Core resolves it in the decoder: DecodeScript does 'auto key = ctx.FromPKHBytes(in[2]...); if (!key) return {};' and stores the key in the PK_H node (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:2331-2339), and for the signer that context is WshSatisfier::FromPKHBytes -> Satisfier::CPubFromPKHBytes, which looks the CKeyID up in the SigningProvider and records a missing_pubkeys entry when it is absent (refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:428-436). ProduceInput's PK_H arm therefore has both the key bytes and a signable key (miniscript.h:1252-1256).
consequence: A P2WSH miniscript containing pkh()/pk_h() is never signed by this node even when it holds every private key, while Core signs the same policy normally -- and the wallet still hands out addresses for it and books the coins as balance, so this is the same funds-loss shape as 1141db2b. The signing path is inference-only: compute-input-signatures' P2WSH arm (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:578-591) calls miniscript-stack, which calls ms-from-script on the witnessScript rather than using the descriptor's own parsed node (whose pk_h DOES carry the key expression), so having imported the descriptor does not help. The failure surfaces as the misleading 'witnessScript is not multisig' (rawtransaction.lisp:591). Severity raised from the finder's S2 to S1 on the rubric's funds clause, verified end to end below. The secondary hazard the finder names is real but not currently reachable: if any signer ever returned a signature for the NIL key, the produced witness would carry a Lisp NIL element that serialization is not prepared for.
evidence: Container: /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s2, warm image, build/ga11probe/p5.lisp and p5b.lisp. (1) Through the shipped bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method 'signrawtransactionwithkey' over a P2WSH whose witnessScript is and_v(v:pk(A),pkh(B)) = 2103a34b99...ad76a914a48e80ddd68b1a9ac7b3bdf028b00a1dbf5e450388ac, supplying BOTH private keys: complete:false, errors[0].error 'witnessScript is not multisig'. The pk() control and_v(v:pk(A),pk(B)) with the identical two keys: complete:true. (2) The inference itself: ms-from-script of that script returns a node printing 'and_v(v:pk(03a34b99..),pkh(a48e80ddd68b1a9ac7b3bdf028b00a1dbf5e4503))' whose PK_H sub has :KEYS NIL and a 20-byte :DATA; satisfied with a signer that signs any key, the directly-parsed node gives stack element sizes (64 33 64) and the inferred node gives (64 :NIL-ELEMENT 64) -- the revealed-pubkey element is the Lisp NIL. (3) Full wallet flow on regtest: wsh(and_v(v:pk(WIF_A),pkh(WIF_B))) imported into a private-key wallet (success T), deriveaddresses -> bcrt1qw209fepkpuzfcddlrnw4znqpl88n423ydkur8tg3q94ckf9fdjrqr5hwaf, the funding wallet's own sendtoaddress paid it, the receiving wallet reported getbalance 1.0, and signrawtransactionwithwallet returned complete:false with 'witnessScript is not multisig'; the wsh(and_v(v:pk(A),pk(B))) control in the identical shape returned complete:true. Sources: src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1810-1817, :1505-1509; src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:464-485 and :578-591; src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:489; refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:2331-2339 and :1252-1256; refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:428-436.
fix_shape: Give ms-from-script Core's FromPKHBytes seam. Add a context callback to the decoder -- a special or an ms-satisfier slot carrying a hash160 -> pubkey resolver -- and have the :pk-h arm call it, storing the resolved key in the node's keys list and failing the whole decode when it cannot resolve, exactly as DecodeScript does (miniscript.h:2331-2339); keep the 20-byte hash in :data so script regeneration stays byte-exact. The two callers already hold the map Core's SigningProvider would answer from: compute-input-signatures has pubmap keyed by the 33-byte pubkey (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469), so the resolver is a hash160-keyed index over it, and Core's keymap in the same function is already keyed on hash160 for the P2PKH/P2WPKH arms. Record an unresolvable hash the way Core records missing_pubkeys rather than silently producing a NIL element, and while the arm is being touched make ms-produce-input refuse to build a stack element from a NIL key at all, so the class of bug cannot recur. The same seam is a prerequisite for the tapscript signer of 1141db2b, where Core's TapSatisfier::FromPKHBytes must resolve Hash160(XOnlyPubKey) rather than the 33-byte key id (refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:514-518).
